accuracy.reason: Separates lifetime, freshness, and space pressure without promising residency or automatic refresh.

evidence.quote: TTL limits an entry's lifetime, not the age of the source data used to fill it.

mechanisms.reason: Explains the distinct removal triggers and connects expiration to later reader-driven refill.

evidence.quote: Sets how long an entry may remain before it expires. A 60-second TTL does not refresh the product every minute; a later miss must load it again.

coherence.reason: Reuses prior product and miss flow to explain the consequences of entries disappearing.

evidence.quote: A product can be evicted before its TTL ends. Some configurations reject new entries when full instead of evicting existing ones.

decisions.reason: Adequately supports distinguishing retention limits and capacity behavior for the target objective; does not teach how to choose TTL values, which is beyond this objective.

evidence.quote: Removes entries to make room. A least-recently-used policy favors removing entries that have not been read recently.

clarity.reason: Defines each term, gives a time example, and explicitly corrects the common timer-as-refresh misconception.

evidence.quote: Sets how long an entry may remain before it expires. A 60-second TTL does not refresh the product every minute; a later miss must load it again.

outcomes.reason: All criteria supported: stale 09:02 hit, expired 09:06 miss, evicted 09:04 miss, distinct time/capacity removals, no lifetime freshness or residency guarantee, and later API-driven refill. The exact quotes support each conclusion.

sourceChecks.claim: Reusable copies reduce repeated work and may diverge from their source.
Application reads and fills on a miss; writes followed by invalidation do not guarantee consistency.
Memory policies can remove entries with remaining TTL or reject new writes; LRU favors entries not accessed recently.
